instructions.rules:
DRIVING POLICY. Choose the next native input by executing the supplied policy exactly. Apply the following fixed bearing policy to the CURRENT factual state; its eligible wheel and pedal form one native input. These are supplied engineering rules, not a claim that the input is optimal or pursuit-equivalent. Read x=ego_x_m and y=ego_y_m from the wheel_facts.road.preview row whose ahead_m equals 15, using wheel_facts.road.preview_columns. The 15 m centre bearing theta equals round(degrees(atan2(y,x)),4), calculated from those rounded raw coordinates. If wheel_facts.road.preview_15m_bearing_deg is present, read theta directly from that factual scalar; otherwise compute theta yourself. Positive theta means LEFT of the kart nose, negative theta means RIGHT. Thresholds are -22, -7, +7 and +22 degrees; exact threshold ties choose the smaller absolute wheel angle. 
WHEEL TASK: Select the single allowed absolute wheel ID whose supplied policy condition holds. Return only that wheel choice.

wheel_facts.units: m,s; display angles deg, handling angles rad. Positive steering/yaw/curvature/ego y/offset are LEFT; ego x forward. Wheel angle is actual; control is held input. road_vs_kart=road tangent minus kart heading. road_turn=future tangent minus current ROAD tangent. Preview distances are centreline arc from nearest projection. Edge clearance<0 is outside. Need=v²×|curvature|; grip ratio>1 exceeds current surface grip. Grip radius excludes steering limits/transients.

criteria.hard_right: Hold wheels RIGHT at 6.88 degrees; a nominal bicycle turn radius of 14.9 metres before grip/response transients. FIXED POLICY ELIGIBILITY: choose this wheel exactly when theta < -22 degrees.
criteria.right: Hold wheels RIGHT at 3.44 degrees; a nominal bicycle turn radius of 30.0 metres before grip/response transients. FIXED POLICY ELIGIBILITY: choose this wheel exactly when -22 <= theta < -7 degrees.
criteria.straight: Hold wheels STRAIGHT at 0.00 degrees; a straight nominal path before grip/response transients. FIXED POLICY ELIGIBILITY: choose this wheel exactly when -7 <= theta <= +7 degrees.
criteria.left: Hold wheels LEFT at 3.44 degrees; a nominal bicycle turn radius of 30.0 metres before grip/response transients. FIXED POLICY ELIGIBILITY: choose this wheel exactly when +7 < theta <= +22 degrees.
criteria.hard_left: Hold wheels LEFT at 6.88 degrees; a nominal bicycle turn radius of 14.9 metres before grip/response transients. FIXED POLICY ELIGIBILITY: choose this wheel exactly when theta > +22 degrees.

instructions.rules:
DRIVING POLICY. Choose the next native input by executing the supplied policy exactly. Apply the following fixed bearing policy to the CURRENT factual state; its eligible wheel and pedal form one native input. These are supplied engineering rules, not a claim that the input is optimal or pursuit-equivalent. Let speed=pedal_facts.kart.speed_m_s and L=pedal_facts.current_road_frame.velocity_left_m_s. Let B be true exactly when pedal_facts.road.on_road is false, OR (pedal_facts.road.offset_m>0 AND pedal_facts.road.left_edge_clearance_m<=3 AND L>=0.5), OR (pedal_facts.road.offset_m<0 AND pedal_facts.road.right_edge_clearance_m<=3 AND L<=-0.5). Otherwise B is false. The speed<2 acceleration rule takes priority even when B is true.
FIXED WORKED PEDAL EXAMPLES (speed and L in m/s, distances in metres; never the current query's answer): on_road=true, offset_m=-10, left_edge_clearance_m=22, right_edge_clearance_m=2, L=+1, speed=8: right-side clearance is small but velocity is inward; B=false -> accelerate. on_road=true, offset_m=+10, left_edge_clearance_m=2, right_edge_clearance_m=22, L=-1, speed=8: left-side clearance is small but velocity is inward; B=false -> accelerate. on_road=true, offset_m=-10, left_edge_clearance_m=22, right_edge_clearance_m=2, L=-1, speed=8: all three right-side predicates hold; B=true -> brake. on_road=true, offset_m=+10, left_edge_clearance_m=2, right_edge_clearance_m=22, L=+1, speed=8: all three left-side predicates hold; B=true -> brake. on_road=false, speed=0: low-speed priority -> accelerate. on_road=false, speed=4: B=true -> coast. on_road=false, speed=8: B=true -> brake.
PEDAL TASK: Select the single allowed pedal ID whose supplied policy condition holds. Return only that pedal choice; the wheel is selected separately in this same request.

pedal_facts.units: m,s; display angles deg, handling angles rad. Positive steering/yaw/curvature/ego y/offset are LEFT; ego x forward. Wheel angle is actual; control is held input. road_vs_kart=road tangent minus kart heading. road_turn=future tangent minus current ROAD tangent. Preview distances are centreline arc from nearest projection. Edge clearance<0 is outside. Need=v²×|curvature|; grip ratio>1 exceeds current surface grip. Grip radius excludes steering limits/transients.

current_road_frame.units: Angles are degrees and velocities are m/s in the CURRENT ROAD frame. Positive nose_vs_road_deg and velocity_vs_road_deg mean LEFT of the current road tangent. Positive velocity_left_m_s means LEFT; positive velocity_forward_m_s means FORWARD along that tangent.

criteria.accelerate: ACCELERATE: throttle 1, brake 0. FIXED POLICY ELIGIBILITY: choose ACCELERATE exactly when speed<2 OR (speed>=2 AND B is false).
criteria.coast: COAST: throttle 0, brake 0. FIXED POLICY ELIGIBILITY: choose COAST exactly when B is true AND 2<=speed<=6.
criteria.brake: BRAKE: throttle 0, brake 1. FIXED POLICY ELIGIBILITY: choose BRAKE exactly when B is true AND speed>6.

instructions.rules: This is a solo kart-racing game. Complete three laps by crossing all 120 required checkpoint gates in order, as quickly as possible while staying on the road. Gates require a forward crossing within their road span. Physics continues in real time while the next decision is requested. Both selected settings form one direct input held until another input is applied. Wheel settings are absolute angles, not increments. After three continuous seconds off-road, rescue returns the kart near its departure point, stopped and coasting, with no checkpoint credit. Choose the next input using the current measurements and the physical control descriptions. wheel_facts.road.preview contains the road centreline point 15 metres of centreline arc ahead of the nearest road projection. Its ego_x_m is forward and ego_y_m is left of the current kart nose. preview_15m_bearing_deg is degrees(atan2(ego_y_m,ego_x_m)) from those rounded coordinates: positive is left of the nose, negative is right. Select one absolute wheel setting to hold next. The pedal is selected in the other question in this same request. Return only the wheel choice.

Preview distances are centreline arc from nearest projection. Edge clearance<0 is outside. Need=v²×|curvature|; grip ratio>1 exceeds current surface grip. Grip radius excludes steering limits/transients.
